questions.desired_improvement: Resolve the explicitly stated planar (1,1,2)-terminal case with an exact polynomial-time algorithm; randomized polynomial time with a standard per-instance success probability of at least 2/3 qualifies.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Bentert et al. (ICALP 2024), Theorem 1: planar Two-Sets Cut-Uncut is solvable by a one-sided-error randomized algorithm in 2^(|S|+|T|) n^O(1) time, but the paper explicitly leaves the three-set planar case with two singleton sets and one two-vertex set open. Fixed-k planar Multiway Cut is polynomial, but it does not impose this uncut connectivity constraint.
questions.forecast_statement: I expect this exact planar three-set case to receive a correct polynomial-time algorithm by the deadline, but regard that outlook as highly uncertain.

items: G is a finite simple undirected planar graph, given without requiring a fixed embedding.
S1={s}, S2={t}, and S3={a,b} are pairwise disjoint; all edge deletion costs are one.
A feasible edge set F leaves s, t, and the connected component containing a and b in three pairwise distinct connected components of G-F; a and b must remain connected.
The objective is to minimize |F|; infeasible instances must be detected.
The event concerns an exact algorithm, not a heuristic, approximation, empirical implementation, or the general nonplanar problem.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two independent reviewers inspect the dated primary source and full proof/algorithm against every frozen assumption. A mismatched graph class, terminal pattern, weighted variant only, or relaxation is not a match. A proof of infeasibility handling and exactness is required. A search miss is not a negative; if no matching source is found by deadline, record INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE unless the separately documented source-coverage review supports an explicit unresolved-at-horizon record.
questions.problem_statement: For an unweighted planar graph G and pairwise disjoint terminal sets S1={s}, S2={t}, S3={a,b}, can the minimum number of edges whose deletion separates every pair of distinct terminal sets while keeping the two terminals in S3 connected be computed in polynomial time?
questions.required_evidence_standard: A dated peer-reviewed article or public preprint containing a complete mathematical algorithm and correctness proof; two independent human reviewers must agree after checking the formal problem statement and proof. LLM review is not an independent reviewer.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2030-12-31, a publicly accessible primary theorem gives an exact polynomial-time algorithm for the specified planar unweighted Three-Sets Cut-Uncut problem, with runtime polynomial in |V(G)|+|E(G)| and success probability at least 2/3 on every input if randomized. The algorithm must either return the optimum cut size and a realizing edge set or correctly report infeasibility. A special case, approximation, or algorithm that drops the requirement that a and b remain connected does not count.

questions.desired_improvement: Improve the current tilde-O(n^(14/3)) exponent to an exact O(n^4 polylog n) algorithm, matching the exponent of the conditional n^(4-o(1)) lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Bringmann, Künnemann, and Nusser give a tilde-O(n^(14/3)) algorithm and a conditional n^(4-o(1)) lower bound under SETH. The exact 2D discrete problem remains between these exponents in the audited sources. The 2025 SoCG result improves one-dimensional translation/scaling variants and uses the known offline grid-reachability routine; it does not establish the 2D discrete event.
questions.forecast_statement: I judge an O(n^4 polylog n) exact algorithm for the unrestricted 2D discrete translation problem unlikely by the deadline.

items: Both input curves have n vertices in R^2; the translation is unrestricted in R^2.
The endpoint is the exact discrete Frechet distance value, not only a fixed-threshold decision problem unless the source proves the stated value bound.

The result must state its computational and arithmetic model; independent adjudication checks material comparability with the exact models used by the baseline papers rather than assuming all real-RAM/algebraic conventions are interchangeable.
No input restrictions beyond those in the cited baseline are allowed.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two independent reviewers verify the source's problem variant, dimension, exactness, model, and full runtime derivation. The event is achieved only if the theorem yields O(n^4 log^C n) for a fixed C. A later conditional lower bound alone does not achieve the event. No matching result by the deadline is not a verified negative without the coverage protocol; otherwise retain INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
questions.problem_statement: Can the exact discrete Frechet distance under translation between two n-vertex polygonal curves in the Euclidean plane be computed in O(n^4 polylog n) worst-case time under computation-model and arithmetic assumptions explicitly shown to be comparable to the published bounds?
questions.required_evidence_standard: Public peer-reviewed or preprint theorem with complete algorithm and asymptotic proof, independently checked by two human reviewers. Benchmark speed is irrelevant to this theorem event.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-10-16, a public primary source proves an exact worst-case O(n^4 log^C n) algorithm for computing discrete Frechet distance under translation for two planar polygonal curves of n vertices each, for some fixed constant C. The theorem must state its computation model and arithmetic assumptions, and an independent reviewer must verify that they are no stronger in a material way than those underlying the cited baseline bounds; if comparability is unclear, the event is unresolved. A decision algorithm qualifies only if a stated reduction yields the same bound for exact value computation. Approximation, one-dimensional curves, continuous Frechet distance, or a restricted input family does not count.

questions.desired_improvement: Remove the high-girth hypothesis from the cited 3k-round upper bound without worsening its asymptotic approximation ratio or model.
questions.existing_strongest_baseline: Lenzen and Wenning (SSS 2024; arXiv 2024) prove a 3k-round O(k+f(k)^(k/(k+1))) approximation for k-hop dominating set under girth at least 4k+3 and k-hop expansion at most f(k), with upper bounds in the port-numbering model with small messages. They explicitly ask whether the high-girth restriction is an artefact or the bound extends to all graphs of bounded k-hop expansion.
questions.forecast_statement: I consider removal of the high-girth restriction at the same bound unlikely by the deadline, while recognizing that the question is explicit and technically active.

items: k-hop domination means every vertex is at graph distance at most k from a selected vertex; objective is minimum cardinality.
The graph family has the cited k-hop expansion bound f(k), interpreted using the shallow-minor/contraction density definition in the primary source.
The algorithm operates in the source's deterministic port-numbering model with small messages; for each fixed k the 3k+O(1) round limit is constant in n.
No minimum-girth condition or other omitted structural restriction is allowed.
The approximation factor must be O(k+f(k)^(k/(k+1))) with a universal hidden constant; it cannot hide dependence on n or girth.

questions.outcome_adjudication_policy: Two independent reviewers check the algorithm model, round count, approximation factor, expansion definition, and absence of any girth condition in the theorem hypotheses. A theorem for a narrower class or with weaker ratio is partial progress only. A search miss is not a negative; absent complete source coverage use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
questions.problem_statement: Can the constant-round k-hop dominating-set approximation bound proved for high-girth graphs of bounded k-hop expansion be achieved on all graphs of the same bounded k-hop expansion, without a girth assumption?
questions.required_evidence_standard: Dated public primary theorem and full proof, independently checked by two human reviewers; simulations and benchmark evidence do not qualify.

resolution_criteria.candidate_criterion: By 2031-10-16, a public primary theorem gives a deterministic LOCAL/port-numbering algorithm using at most 3k+O(1) rounds and small messages which, for every fixed integer k>=1 and every graph family whose k-hop expansion is bounded by f(k), computes a k-hop dominating set of size at most C*(k+f(k)^(k/(k+1)))*OPT on every graph in the family, for a universal constant C, with no girth assumption. A restricted girth class, randomized-only theorem, or asymptotically worse ratio does not count.
